newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil telecom bill clears Senate committees.
newsitem.headline: Brazil telecom bill clears Senate committees.

text.p: A bill which paves the way for the privatization of Brazil's telecommunications industry was approved by three Senate committees Tuesday, a congressional official said.
The committees still had to vote on several proposed amendments to the bill before it advanced to the floor of the Senate for a final vote in Congress, the official said.
Government whips were also expected to propose a motion which would allow the bill, called the General Telecommunications Law, to be put to its full Senate vote later this week.
The government wants to approve the bill quickly to allow for the privatization of the federally owned Telebras system set to begin early 1998.
The bill does not set any limits on foreign capital in Brazilian telecommunications operators, but gives the president of the republic powers to limit non-Brazilian investors on a case-by-case basis.
The law would also create a new regulator and set down rules for private companies operating in the sector.
